decision: Use a minimal qrexec service wrapper around the already-authenticated durable process coordinator, with one OS process per qrexec-style call in the contract test.

criteria.correctness: Preserves the signed-envelope and durable-journal semantics already covered by recovery tests; no second protocol/state machine.
criteria.robustness: Fails closed unless store, journal, and >=32-byte transport secret are all present; process-per-call testing exercises restart boundaries naturally.
criteria.latency: Only adds process/qrexec launch overhead; no extra network service or database round trip.
criteria.resourceUse: Small transient Node process, no daemon or external infrastructure.
criteria.regressionRisk: Low because orchestration and reconciliation logic remain in runProcessCoordinator.
criteria.qa: Synthetic contract test verifies fail-closed configuration, cross-process retry equality, durable state visibility, and tamper rejection. Real Qubes/qrexec execution remains a separate gate.

alternatives.name: new-qrexec-specific-protocol
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Duplicates authentication/replay/reconciliation logic and increases semantic drift/regression risk.

alternatives.name: long-running-network-daemon-between-qubes
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Adds listening surface, lifecycle complexity, memory use, and unnecessary transport exposure versus native qrexec stdin/stdout.

alternatives.name: external-transactional-database-before-qrexec
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Potentially stronger multi-host atomicity later, but higher operational latency and resource cost before the VM-boundary transport is proven.

lessons: Transport adaptation should not own mission semantics.
A qrexec service should fail closed when durability or authentication configuration is missing.
Process-per-call retries are a useful local approximation of qrexec lifecycle behavior, but they do not prove Qubes policy, VM identity, or real qrexec latency.

CI run 42 failed twice because the new qrexec fixture searched for a non-contract mission.agent field. The runtime contract identifies agents through metadata.agentId and requiredCapabilities. Fix the fixture rather than adding a redundant production field solely to satisfy a test.
When an integration test crosses subsystem boundaries, assertions should target documented persisted/runtime fields, not convenience shapes invented by the fixture.
safety: Synthetic/defensive orchestration only; no real financial operations or payment data.
